description: Safe cleanup and normalization rules. These rules change format, grammar, spelling, and language register only. Facts are never changed. If a value is too vague to translate safely, it is left for the evaluator to flag.

time.description: Normalize time values to 24-hour HHMM hours format. Always preserve 'approximately' when the officer used it or when approximation is implied.

conversions.output_format: HHMM hours (e.g., '1800 hours', '1830 hours', '2030 hours', '0830 hours')

non_numeric_descriptors.action: Return as-is. Evaluator will flag RED — non-numeric time descriptor is a red blocker. Do not attempt to guess a time.

time.prefix: Always output 'at approximately [TIME] hours' — preserve or add 'approximately'.

rank.description: Normalize rank abbreviations to fully spelled-out titles. Apply to both officer rank and OIC rank fields.
rank.rule: Match case-insensitively. Output the fully spelled-out rank in title case.

name_and_title.description: All proper names to title case. Fix known spelling errors in rank titles.
rules: Convert all-lowercase names to title case: 'john smith' → 'John Smith'
Convert all-caps names to title case: 'JOHN SMITH' → 'John Smith'
Common rank spelling corrections are handled by the rank map above
Do not change hyphenated names: 'Smith-Jones' stays 'Smith-Jones'
Do not alter DC numbers: 'A12345' stays 'A12345'

location.description: Use exact location in Paragraph 1. Use broader operational area in Paragraph 3. Never write 'orderly operation of [cell number].'
rules: Paragraph 1 exact location: 'cell E3107', 'the Wing 2 dayroom', 'the shower area'
Paragraph 3 operational area: 'E Dorm', 'Wing 2', 'the housing unit' — never 'cell E3107'
If officer provides only a cell number with no dorm/area, prompt for the dorm separately via YELLOW warning

order.description: Convert officer's description of giving the order into the command itself only. Remove all first-person phrasing.

examples.input: I told him to go back to his cell
I ordered him to cuff up
I told him to stop kicking the door
I told him to sit down

examples.output: stop (VAGUE — evaluator will flag RED: stop what?)

order.rule: If after removing the first-person prefix the remaining command is a single word or clearly vague, return the cleaned version. The evaluator will detect vagueness and flag RED.
order.do_not_invent: If the officer's phrasing is too vague to translate accurately, leave the cleaned version for the evaluator to flag. Do not invent specific commands.

inmate_before_order.description: Goal: observable language that shows what the officer saw before any words were spoken.
bad_input_patterns: he wouldn't go in his cell
inmate_before_order.action_for_bad_input: Return as-is with flag for evaluator. Do not rewrite inmate behavior. The evaluator will surface a YELLOW warning for conclusory or too-vague inmate behavior.
acceptable_output_examples: standing at the cell door outside of his assigned cell
remaining outside of his assigned cell during count procedures
remaining stationary outside of his assigned bunk area
blocking the cell doorway without moving toward his assigned bunk
remaining in the shower area after scheduled shower time

acknowledgment.description: Convert informal acknowledgment descriptions to standard acknowledgment sentence phrasing.

map.input: she was standing right in front of me

quote.description: Exact quotes only inside quotation marks. Do not put summaries inside quotation marks.
rules: Preserve all words inside the quote exactly — do not change any words
Fix capitalization of the first word in the quote
Add terminal punctuation if missing (period or exclamation mark)
Preserve profanity exactly as the officer reported it — do not sanitize
If officer provides a description of what was said rather than exact words, leave for evaluator to flag YELLOW (quote is summary)

tone.description: Normalize tone descriptors. Remove over-stacked tone lists. Remove conclusion-based tone language.
rules: Do not use 'non-compliant tone' as the only tone descriptor — it is a legal conclusion, not a description of how something sounded
Do not stack more than three tone descriptors
Profane is acceptable only if the exact quote provided by the officer contains profanity
If over-stacked, trim to the most specific two or three descriptors

physical_behavior.description: Separate visual behavior from auditory behavior. Convert conclusions to observable actions.
rules: Visual behavior (what the officer saw) goes in one sentence
Auditory behavior (how something sounded) goes in a separate sentence
Wrong: 'Inmate Smith stood aggressively in a loud manner'
Right: 'Inmate Smith crossed his arms and remained positioned at the cell door. Inmate Smith raised his voice in a loud and argumentative manner audible to surrounding inmates.'
If officer provides a duration without an observable action, leave for evaluator to flag YELLOW
Convert conclusions to observable actions when the observable action is clearly implied and not invented
Do not invent physical behavior — if not observable from the officer's description, leave for evaluator

operational_impact.description: Translate vague operational impact language into specific FDOC report language. Reference dorm/wing/area only — never cell number.

map.output: temporarily interrupting the master roster count
temporarily interrupting the master roster count
drawing the attention of surrounding inmates
drawing the attention of surrounding inmates

map.input: pulled me away from what I was doing
map.output: requiring staff attention away from normal duties

operational_impact.minimum_impact_template: This incident occurred during [OFFICER ACTIVITY] in [AREA], requiring this officer's immediate attention away from assigned duties.
operational_impact.area_rule: Always reference dorm, wing, or facility area — never cell number in operational impact sentence

ability_and_force.description: Default output when no issue and no force. Do not apply default if officer reported any issue.
ability_and_force.default_no_issue_no_force: Inmate [LAST NAME] displayed no apparent medical condition, mental health issue, physical limitation, or language barrier that would have prevented compliance with this officer's directive. No use of force was required.
ability_and_force.forbidden: Do not say 'there was nothing wrong with him/her/them.'

pronoun_and_reference.description: Apply narrative reference style consistently across all six paragraphs.
pronoun_and_reference.charge_advisory_rule: Never repeat the last name twice in the same sentence in the charge advisory. Use the pronoun matching the narrative reference style.
pronoun_and_reference.bad_example: due to Smith's failure to comply, Smith will be receiving
pronoun_and_reference.good_example: due to his failure to comply with a direct order, he would receive

confinement.description: Normalize confinement language. Convert disciplinary confinement to administrative confinement when used before a hearing.

disciplinary_to_administrative.trigger: Officer types 'disciplinary confinement' in the confinement field before a hearing has occurred
disciplinary_to_administrative.action: Convert to 'administrative confinement' and return YELLOW note
disciplinary_to_administrative.yellow_note: Note: Disciplinary confinement is a post-hearing sanction. Pre-hearing placement is administrative confinement. This has been corrected in the report.

templates.placed: Inmate [LAST NAME] was placed in administrative confinement pending the outcome of this disciplinary report.
templates.remained: Inmate [LAST NAME] remained in administrative confinement pending the outcome of this disciplinary report.

typo_correction.description: Correct all obvious typos silently without flagging unless the correction changes meaning.
